dimensions.assessment: Affects state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies, retired officers seeking employment, and the Department of Justice.
dimensions.evidence: eligible entity means a State, local, Tribal, or territorial law enforcement agency

dimensions.assessment: Provides grant funding opportunities and mandates strict disciplinary record checks and annual Inspector General audits for participating agencies.
dimensions.evidence: conducting a search of the National Decertification Index; or requesting the personnel record

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes grant funding and audit administration through the Department of Justice without specifying total aggregate authorization amounts.
dimensions.evidence: The Attorney General may award grants to eligible entities

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to create a new grant program with accountability and auditing rules.
dimensions.evidence: Title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (34 U.S.C. 10101 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing grant authorities and permanent annual audit and certification requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning in the first fiscal year beginning after the date of enactment ... and in each fiscal year thereafter

missing_information: Total authorized appropriation amounts or funding caps for the grant program.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a Department of Justice grant program for state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to hire retired personnel for civilian tasks and training, accompanied by audit requirements and disciplinary record checks.

card.summary: S. 2296, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, sets policies, authorities, and funding levels for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and Department of Energy national security programs. It also incorporates numerous specific acts concerning intelligence activities, coast guard operations, maritime systems, housing reforms, and state department authorizations.
